sections.h2: Who runs property tax in Sangamon County?
sections.html:
The county treasurer bills and collects, the Supervisor of Assessments and the Board of Review handle values and appeals, and the county clerk takes over once taxes are sold. Most of this happens in the County Building at 200 South Ninth Street in Springfield, the county seat and the state capital.

  • Treasurer: first floor, Room 109, with weekday hours of 8:30 to 5:00, phone (217) 753-6800 for programs and deferral questions.
  • Supervisor of Assessments: phone (217) 753-6805. This office issues parcel numbers, exemption forms and complaint forms.
  • County Clerk: phone (217) 753-6701. It issues estimates of redemption on sold taxes.
  • Recorder: 200 South Ninth Street, first floor, phone (217) 535-3150, for deeds.

The county's property tax website lets you look up a parcel by number, address or owner, view the current billing details, and print exemption and complaint forms. The county covers 868 square miles of land and holds 26 active townships, one of which, Capital Township, covers the same ground as the City of Springfield.

sections.h2: What was the 2026 payment schedule for Sangamon County?
sections.html:
For 2025 taxes payable in 2026, the first installment was due June 5 and the second September 4, 2026. The treasurer's published schedule had the property tax sale on November 6, 2026, which means any 2025 tax unpaid by then moved to the sale.

  • E-check, credit and debit card, phone and drive-thru payments ran through November 4, 2026 at 5:00 p.m.
  • The last day to pay in the Treasurer's office was November 5, 2026 at 5:00 p.m., with cash or check only that day.
  • E-check on the county site carries no fee, while card payments add a convenience fee charged by the card companies.
  • Phone payments by card go through (888) 834-3729. Mailed checks go to the Sangamon County Collector, PO Box 19400, Springfield, IL 62794-9400, and must be postmarked by the due date.

The treasurer states that all payments are assessed a late penalty after their due dates. The same two-installment pattern repeats each year, with the first installment in early summer and the second in early fall, so look at the tentative dates the treasurer posts every spring.

sections.h2: When is the deadline to appeal a Sangamon County assessment?
sections.html:
The deadline depends on your township, because the county publishes assessment changes township by township and sets a separate complaint deadline for each, roughly a month after publication. For 2026 the deadlines fall anywhere from early September to late December.

sections.h2: What exemptions does Sangamon County offer homeowners?
sections.html:
The Supervisor of Assessments lists the general homestead exemption, a senior exemption, a senior assessment freeze, an improvement exemption, and several veteran and disability exemptions.

  • General Homestead: up to $6,000 off equalized assessed value for an owner-occupied home. The application deadline is January 31 for the tax year, and no yearly renewal is needed. It does not move with you, so a new home needs a new application.
  • Senior Citizen: $5,000 off for owners 65 or older, filed by January 31.
  • Senior Citizen Assessment Freeze: household income of $75,000 or less, with ownership and occupancy for at least a year before applying. Forms are available between April 1 and July 1, and the deadline is July 1 each year.
  • Homestead Improvement: new additions, garages, decks or porches can add up to $75,000 of market value with no tax increase for up to four years.
  • Disabled Persons: $2,000 off, with annual renewal. Returning Veterans: $5,000 off.

The treasurer also describes a senior deferral program that places a lien on the home, with deferred taxes due when the property is sold or the owner dies. Anyone selling a home with a deferral should ask the treasurer for a payoff.

sections.h2: What happens if Sangamon County property tax is not paid?
sections.html:
The taxes are sold at the annual sale, and you pay them off through the County Clerk instead of the Treasurer. The clerk gives an estimate of redemption on request at (217) 753-6701, and the redemption figure includes late fees, interest and tax sale fees.

Sold taxes must be paid with certified funds, a cashier's check, a money order or cash, made out to the Sangamon County Clerk. Personal and business checks and credit cards are not accepted for them. The clerk's office also notes that you may contact the tax buyer directly and ask whether they will take payments, but if the buyer refuses, you pay through the clerk.

Current-year taxes are different: they can be paid with a personal check or cash to the County Treasurer and Collector. For a duplicate bill, contact the treasurer. A tax buyer registers through the treasurer before the sale.

sections.h2: What is Sangamon County like for homeowners and sellers?
sections.html:
Sangamon County sits near the center of Illinois, was formed in 1821, and takes its name from the Sangamon River. It had 196,343 residents at the 2020 census, and the Census Bureau estimated 194,170 in July 2025. About 81% of residents lived in urban areas in 2020.

Census figures give $176,300 as the middle value of an owner-occupied home, median gross rent at $983, and median household income at $75,357. Owners live in 71.3% of homes. The county has 93,820 housing units and issued 224 building permits in 2025.

School districts with territory in the county include Springfield District 186, Ball-Chatham, Rochester, Pleasant Plains and Williamsville. Interstates 55 and 72 and U.S. 36 cross the county. January lows average about 17 degrees and July highs about 87, with May the wettest month.

sections.h2: How does a Sangamon County deed get recorded?
sections.html:
Each sale or gift needs a new deed that is prepared, signed, notarized and recorded with the Sangamon County Recorder. A sale of $100 or more also needs a PTAX-203 filed with the deed so transfer tax can be collected.

The recorder's fee schedule prints a standard recording fee of $64 for a deed on 8.5 by 11 paper with a 3 by 5 inch blank space in the upper right corner, and $84 for a non-standard document. Transfer tax stamps are priced at $0.50 per $500 of value for the state plus $0.25 per $500 for the county. A gift is exempt if the deed carries the exemption paragraph. The office aims to return mailed originals in three to five business days, and eRecording is available through title companies and other vendors.

sections.h2: Can I sell a Sangamon County house with taxes owed?
sections.html:
Yes, a house with taxes owed can be sold, but you need two numbers first: the current amount from the treasurer and an estimate of redemption from the County Clerk for any sold year.

  • Look up the parcel on the county's property tax website for billing details.
  • Ask the clerk whether any earlier year was sold, and for the payoff.
  • Confirm whether a senior freeze or deferral applies, since a deferral is repaid on sale.

Pass the figures to the title company so the payoff is handled at the closing table. A house needing repairs and carrying back taxes may find a cash buyer who takes it in present condition.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Sangamon County property taxes?
faqs.a: Pay the Sangamon County Treasurer online by e-check, by phone at (888) 834-3729, by mail to PO Box 19400, Springfield, IL 62794-9400, or in person in Room 109 of the County Building. E-check carries no fee. Card payments carry a convenience fee.

faqs.q: When did the 2026 installments come due in Sangamon County?
faqs.a: The first installment was due June 5, 2026 and the second September 4, 2026. The treasurer set the last day to pay in the office at November 5, 2026, and the tax sale for November 6. Check the treasurer's page each spring for the next dates.

faqs.q: How do I get an estimate to redeem sold taxes in Sangamon County?
faqs.a: Call the County Clerk at (217) 753-6701 and ask for an estimate of redemption. Pay with certified funds, a cashier's check, a money order or cash made payable to the Sangamon County Clerk. Credit cards and personal checks are not accepted.

faqs.q: Does the general homestead exemption move to a new house?
faqs.a: No, it stays with the property. The Supervisor of Assessments says the exemption does not transfer, so a buyer who lives in the home files a new application. The deadline is January 31 for the tax year, and the exemption takes up to $6,000 off assessed value.

faqs.q: Which Sangamon County office files my deed?
faqs.a: File it with the Sangamon County Recorder on the first floor of the County Building, 200 South Ninth Street in Springfield, phone (217) 535-3150. Include a PTAX-203 for a sale of $100 or more. Mailed originals can be sent with a check for the exact fee.
